% Beamer source, in the shape the real course decks use: \date{} empty, the
% subtitle folded into \title after a \\, and the "Material adapted from" block
% as free-standing centred text INSIDE the title frame, after \maketitle.
%
% C-TITLEPAGE was originally filed because that trailing block printed ON TOP of
% the title under ltx-talk 0.5.0. THAT SYMPTOM IS GONE -- it did not reproduce on
% 0.5.3 (2026-08-24) or 0.6.2 (2026-09-11), against a one-line attribution, a long
% multi-line block, a no-\vfill variant and \maketitle outside any frame.
%
% So the conversion keeps this construct rather than working around it: see
% after.tex, whose title block differs from this one in exactly two ways, both
% forced and both still valid beamer. naive.tex is the hand-rolled title frame
% the skill used to recommend, and what that costs.
\documentclass{beamer}

\author[A. Lecturer]{A. Lecturer\\ \texttt{a.l@uni.ac.uk}}
\institute[Somewhere]{University of Somewhere}
\title[CSP]{Constraint Satisfaction\\\large{Backtracking and arc consistency}}
\date{}

\begin{document}
\begin{frame}
	\maketitle
	\vspace{-4em}
	\begin{center}
		Material adapted from: \\
		Russell and Norvig (AIMA Book): Chapter 6
	\end{center}
\end{frame}
\end{document}
